title: Per-head outlier-aware KV quantization calibration and latency/quality profiling
creator: Maya Gonzalez
description: Experiment to develop and validate a per-attention-head KV cache quantization calibration pipeline that identifies per-head outliers and applies asymmetric clipping + per-head scaling to improve INT8/FP8 accuracy while preserving low tail latency. Goal is to produce deployable quant profiles and a runtime gating rule that switches precision or clipping thresholds based on observed activation distributions.
background_and_motivation: Previous KV quant sweeps used layer-wise or global clipping which leaves some attention heads with heavy outliers that dominate reconstruction error when using INT8 or experimental FP8 formats. We believe head-level statistics will allow substantially tighter dynamic ranges for the majority of heads while isolating a small set of 'outlier heads' that need wider range or higher precision. This should reduce average token compute and memory bandwidth requirements for KV while keeping model quality within SLOs.
success_criteria: No more than 2% relative degradation on the canonical eval set (long-form completion prompts) vs FP32 baseline when using INT8 per-head profiles
95th-percentile token latency remains within 1.15x of baseline runtime for the same batching configuration
Runtime gating rule reduces high-precision fallbacks to <8% of requests under typical production workload mix
Profiles validated in shadow on dedicated pool and have PR with benchmark artifacts
calibration_plan_steps: Collect per-head activation histograms across representative workloads (short chat, long completion, summarization) using 1M KV samples sampled from production shadow traces
Implement percentile-based clipping per head (configurable percentiles 99.5, 99.9, 99.95) and compute optimal asymmetric scale/zero-point for INT8 and FP8 analog
Run offline reconstruction error and token-logprob drift analysis vs FP32 on held-out eval prompts
Derive candidate per-head profile artifacts (scale, bias, precision flag) and store in profile manifest
Integrate runtime profile selector that can: apply per-head quant during KV encode/decode, or raise precision for heads flagged 'outlier'
End-to-end latency benchmarks on p4d/p3 using production batching distributions
Shadow rollout to 5% of internal traffic with continuous quality monitors and automatic rollback if regression exceeds thresholds
evaluation_metrics: token-level logprob delta vs FP32 (mean/median/95/99 percentiles)
Downstream task metrics (e.g., summarization ROUGE-L, code completion exact match where applicable)
Per-head reconstruction MSE and max-absolute error
Latency p50/p95/p99 per-token and end-to-end completion
Compute and memory bandwidth delta (measured by kernel counters)
initial_results_summary: Early offline runs (INT8 per-head percentile clipping at 99.9) show median logprob delta of +0.8% and mean delta +1.9% vs FP32 on long-form prompts; heads classified as 'outlier' are ~6% of total and account for ~55% of reconstruction error. p95 token latency increased by ~7% on p4d when using per-head quant without runtime gating (acceptable), but p99 increased by 28% in worst-case due to fallback code path; this motivates implementing a lightweight gating mechanism to prefer mixed-precision per-request rather than synchronous fallbacks.
next_steps: Ship a prototype runtime gating rule: fast heuristic based on request sequence length and prefix KL drift estimate to pre-select per-head precision set
Add a compact per-profile checksum and shadow validation harness that runs 1% of requests through FP32 path for drift monitoring
Optimize fallback path to avoid sync stalls (explore async decode of 'outlier' heads at higher precision)
Schedule review with ModelOps and Runtime teams to agree operational rollout criteria (alerts, automatic rollback)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Per-head profiles increase runtime memory/manifest size. Mitigation: compress manifest, only store overrides for non-default heads
Risk: Frequent profile churn from dataset shift. Mitigation: per-profile TTL and drift-triggered recalibration job
Risk: Outlier detection false positives causing quality regressions. Mitigation: shadow validation and conservative initial thresholds
